evidence: TED place-of-performance lists 13 countries (CZE DEU DNK ESP EST FIN FRA GRC ITA LVA POL PRT SWE) and the buyer is the European High-Performance Computing Joint Undertaking, Luxembourg. Our fetcher queries place-of-performance IN (CZE), so the notice legitimately matched; the normalizer then set geo_origin CZ and attributed the whole envelope to Czechia.
impact: 41.2% of the CZ money mass on its own.
note: The published value is real and stays. The defect is ours: a multi-country envelope must not be attributed 100% to whichever country matched the query. Until the normalizer can apportion, this record is excluded from per-geo money aggregates and counted only in EU-level ones.

evidence: TED total-value and estimated-value-lot both state CZK 32,600,232,225. Our conversion at 24.5 CZK/EUR is arithmetically exact (32600232225 / 24.5 = 1330621723). The notice is cn-standard, CPV 72212000 (application software programming services), buyer Ministerstvo obrany, titled 'Maintenance APV a DZ IS GINIS DEFENCE'.
note: Our converter is CORRECT — this was checked and an earlier claim that the conversion was at fault is withdrawn. The dispute is with the published figure: ~32.6bn CZK for maintaining one information system is roughly a fifth of the entire annual Czech defence budget. We consider it a probable unit error by the publisher (a factor of 100 would give ~326m CZK, about EUR 13.3m, which fits the scope) but we have NOT refuted it at source and hold no correction from the buyer. It is therefore recorded as disputed, not as a known error, and excluded from aggregates until resolved.
